findings.summary: The test detects code files with a fixed list of file types
findings.evidence: CODE_EXTENSIONS lists 13 extensions, and CODE_NAMES covers only Cargo.toml and build.rs. A code file of another type (.toml config, .yaml, an extensionless script) would not be caught. The capability itself accepts any file type, so a blocklist is a reasonable approximation. A stricter alternative is an allowlist of data types (json, md, txt).

summary: The change does what was asked, and I recommend it pass. A new test file, crates/athena-core/tests/study_instance_split.rs, is now recorded as the mechanism for OLY-B-S1-02 in docs/spec.toml, with owner Athena and a measure that names the test command and ends `status: not shown`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --test study_instance_split` in the working copy and all 12 tests passed. Run against the real files, the test checks two things: every studies/<id>/ directory has a pin.json and no code file, and the study capability's src/ and prompts/ never name an instance, either by a `studies/<id>` path or by the quoted id. Negative tests show each check catches a code file, a missing pin, an instance named either way, and a wrong measure, owner or mechanism. With the spec entry reverted to the base, Athena's run failed with exit 101, so the test does fail without the mechanism. The spec text also cites `StudyCapability::admit` and `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates`. I read both: they exist, and admit does refuse changes outside a single studies/<id>/ directory. Two parts of the requirement are not checked: each later instance being studied with a fresh context, and gaps being fixed in the capability and re-checked. The test notes and the measure both say so (`status: not shown`), which the accepted reading allows. The fmt, clippy and test checks come from the CI run Athena recorded for this commit; I did not rerun them. There are two minor findings: xtask/shard-timings.txt changed although it is not on the deliverables list, and the test's list of code file types is a fixed blocklist.
